scorecards.inningsCommentary: West Indies commenced their first innings at Queens Sports Club, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 90 from SD Hope, complemented by a commanding 75-run stand between SD Hope and KOA Powell that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.64 RPO. Zimbabwe's bowling response was spearheaded by AG Cremer (4/64), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Folded for 219/10 (82.5 ov), West Indies suffered an early setback, conceding vital first-innings momentum to Zimbabwe.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Zimbabwe embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 434 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 73 from BRM Taylor, complemented by a commanding 99-run stand between H Masakadza and SF Mire that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.47 RPO. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by D Bishoo (5/105), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 316/10 (90.4 ov), Zimbabwe succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as West Indies's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Queens Sports Club commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 219/10 (82.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Zimbabwe countered with 159/10 (61.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 92-Run Stand: D Bishoo & RL Chase, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, D Bishoo delivered a masterclass for West Indies (44 Runs & 10 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 57%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Zimbabwe faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by RL Chase (126 Runs & 3 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 117 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Zimbabwe produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
